scope: Active voucher creation sites detected by scripts/audit-write-evidence.mjs after excluding updates/deletes/restores/moves of existing voucher rows. Completed phases are retained separately as historical evidence and must not re-enter the active backlog.

explicit-replay-guard.verdict: not a request-identity defect at this creation site
explicit-replay-guard.reason: The creation is protected by an explicit existing-voucher/source-row check, an atomic state claim, conflict handling, or replace-in-transaction semantics. A sequential retry does not leave a second live voucher even though the file bypasses the central posting engine.

migration-import-repair.verdict: reviewed special-purpose path; still outside request-identity enforcement
migration-import-repair.reason: These are migration, import, repair, revaluation, backfill, or administrative conversion paths rather than ordinary posting endpoints. They were reviewed separately because client-request identity is not always the right key; rerunnable ones need a deterministic source/run identity instead.

operational-without-request-identity.reason: These remaining operational creation paths still bypass the canonical posting engine and the Phase 4 durable operational request boundary. They remain the Phase 5 retry/idempotency backlog.

phase-3-infrastructure-writers.verdict: phase 3 completed with required deterministic posting identity
phase-3-infrastructure-writers.reason: These lower-level voucher writers use the durable accounting posting request identity boundary. They require stable business/request source identity, serialize identical concurrent retries, reuse matching vouchers, reject changed payloads under a reused key, and clean identity markers before intentional hard-delete/rebuild operations.

phase-4-operational-writers.verdict: phase 4 completed behind the durable operational request boundary
phase-4-operational-writers.reason: These highest-risk manual voucher, payroll, advance, employee cash/POS and supplier-payment writers are registered behind one company-scoped request boundary. Browser and offline retries reuse a persisted clientRequestId; the server atomically reserves (company, idempotency key), fingerprints method/path/payload, blocks duplicate execution, waits for an identical in-flight request, replays the stored response after completion, rejects changed payloads under the same key, and fails closed when the first outcome is uncertain.
